messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `test_getPackageName_Class` checks that the package name of an array class `String[].class` is "java.lang". The method under test is `ClassUtils.getPackageName(Class<?>)`. The implementation of `getPackageName(Class<?>)` calls `getPackageName(String)` with the class name obtained via `cls.getName()`.

The `getPackageName(String)` method is supposed to extract the package name from a fully qualified class name string. It should handle normal class names as well as array encoding (e.g., class names of array types).

The bug report highlights a failure of a similarly named method `getShortClassName` when handling arrays: the method returns a class name with an appended semicolon (`"String;"`) instead of `"String"`. This suggests that the methods dealing with class names do not correctly strip array-related encoding characters (`[`, `]`, `;`) before extracting the short or package name.

Inspecting `getPackageName(String)` shows the following:
- It finds the last dot (`.`) to separate package and class.
- However, comments hint at "Strip array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding" but no implementation appears to actually do this stripping before taking the substring. This can cause incorrect package name extraction on array classes, whose names include leading '[' characters and trailing ';' for object arrays.

Similarly, `getShortClassName(String)` appears to lack array encoding stripping before extracting the short class name, which can explain the semicolon in the output for arrays reported in the current bug report.

Thus, the root cause is a missing and or incomplete handling of array encoding characters embedded in the class name strings in both `getPackageName` and `getShortClassName` methods. The methods do not currently preprocess the input string to remove these array-related markers, causing incorrect package and short class name results when arrays are input.

This explains the failure of the test expecting "java.lang" for `String[].class` since the array class name string would look like "[Ljava.lang.String;" and the substring logic on it without stripping array syntax would fail to produce the correct package name.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue and don't help explain the failure.

Summary: The problem is that `getPackageName(String)` and also `getShortClassName(String)` do not properly strip the array type encoding from names before extracting package or short class names, leading to wrong results for array class names.

Next, I will suggest methods that should be fixed.
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
